problem: Object-goal navigation in complex domestic environments suffers from spatial memory and semantic uncertainties; instruction-based VLN needs step-by-step instructions, and existing memory is not kept accurate or actionable as the world changes.
motivation: Domestic open-world settings are dynamic, so robots need persistent, updatable multimodal memory that links what they saw, where it was, and what it is. A retrieval-based memory that is continuously evaluated and updated can support semantic reasoning and low-latency decisions on a real quadruped.
key_idea: Build a Dynamic Memory Knowledge Graph that links visual inputs, 3D coordinates and target captions, keep it current with a visual-sampling RAG update and reachability evaluation, and drive navigation with visual PPO-CLIP planning and modality-switching locomotion.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so ablation-level insight cannot be verified. The abstract claims that cross-modal memory with continuous reachability assessment and incremental updates yields more stable semantic associations and better SR and SPL than baselines in Habitat and on a real robot.
method: Dynamic Memory Knowledge Graph (DMKG): integrates visual inputs, 3D spatial coordinates and target captions into a multimodal vector memory for cross-modal correspondence
Visual sampling-based RAG updating evaluation: continuously assesses target reachability and incrementally updates the memory
Semantic retrieval: object navigation by retrieving from the multimodal memory instead of following step-by-step instructions
Visual PPO-CLIP adaptive planning: RL-based planner using CLIP visual features
Visual pattern recognition and modality-switching locomotion control: unified end-to-end pipeline on a quadruped with obstacle avoidance
